headline: Strong ad growth overshadowed by legal charge, severance hit
summary_short: Revenue rose 28% y/y to $60.80B on 14% higher ad impressions and 12% higher average price per ad, but operating income fell 8% to $18.78B and diluted EPS fell 13% to $6.18 as total costs and expenses jumped 55% y/y.
summary_long: Q2 revenue grew 28% y/y to $60.80B (27% ex-FX) on 14% higher ad impressions and 12% higher average price per ad; Family of Apps revenue was $60.37B against a $4.62B Reality Labs operating loss. Costs and expenses rose 55% y/y to $42.03B, including $2.40B of legal-proceedings charges and $1.18B of severance from the May 2026 headcount reduction, pulling operating margin to 31% from 43% and net income down 14% to $15.85B. Capex was $31.08B; free cash flow fell to $784M from $8.55B. Cash and marketable securities were $90.26B against $83.66B of long-term debt. Guidance: Q3 revenue $61-64B; FY26 expenses raised to $165-169B, capex narrowed to $130-145B, tax rate raised to 15-17%.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the increase to ad impressions delivered across Family of Apps rising 14% y/y and average price per ad rising 12% y/y; revenue ex-FX would have grown 27%.
Total costs and expenses rose 55% y/y, which the release attributes to $2.40B of legal-proceedings charges and $1.18B of severance from the May 2026 headcount reduction, on top of higher R&D spend.
Tracks the operating-income decline plus a higher effective tax rate (16% vs 11% a year ago); pre-tax income fell $1.78B and tax expense rose $711M.
EPS fell 13%, roughly tracking the 14% net-income decline; diluted share count was little changed (2,566M vs 2,570M) since Meta did not repurchase stock this quarter.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg framed the quarter as AI "accelerating our core business," while the release itself attributes the margin compression to one-off legal and severance charges rather than the underlying ad business, which grew impressions and pricing.
